per_question.q1: Stem window = the moment of slaking. A: paragraph 2 states it — 'Möter den brända stenen sedan vatten börjar den sjuda, spricker och faller sönder till ett fint vitt mjöl'. 'Fräsa' is in fact the idiomatic Swedish verb for slaking lime, so the synonym shift sjuda→fräste is a lexical improvement, not a stretch, and 'föll sönder till ett … vitt …' tracks the passage's own predicate. B (heat strong enough to ignite dry wood): true of real slaking, which is strongly exothermic, but the passage's only 'hetta' is the thousand-degree BURNING in the sentence before ('När kalksten hettas upp till omkring tusen grader'); nothing about heat, let alone ignition, is predicated of the slaking. Refuted on an 'enligt texten' stem. C (slaked mass laid in pits to mature): lime-putty pit maturation is real practice, and paragraph 6's 'ofta med en grop i mitten' supplies a lexical lure, but that grop is the depression in an overgrown röse, and paragraph 3 fixes the storage stage on the other side of the slaking — 'den brända stenen förvarades torr till dess den skulle släckas och blandas till bruk'. No pit and no maturation stage exists anywhere in the passage. D (mixed with sand while still seething): hot-mixing is real practice, but paragraph 2 orders the events — seethe, crack, fall apart to mjöl, and it is THAT product, 'den släckta kalk som blandad med sand ger murbruk', that meets the sand; paragraph 3 repeats the order in a bare coordination, 'släckas och blandas till bruk'. The simultaneity is the option's own addition. Only A survives.
per_question.q2: A: contradicted head-on by 'En ugn var för stor för ett enskilt hushåll', and nothing licenses the 'efter hand' trajectory. B (a well-off farm owned the kiln and charged): the same sentence pair kills it — 'Den restes och brändes av ett ugnslag – en handfull grannar som sköt till var sin andel ved, turades om vid elden och delade den färdiga kalken efter insats'. Erection is collective, input is per-share, output is divided by insats; no owner and no payer exists. The strongest counsel for B is that 'delade … efter insats' is a kind of settling-up, but that is division among contributors, not purchase from a proprietor. C: contradicted by 'Det mesta av kalken gick till avsalu', and it also answers a different question from the stem. D: stated. Only D survives.
per_question.q3: A: the ranking is inverted in the passage — 'Framför allt var det dit kalken gick: till murningen av stenhus, broar och kyrktorn', while the fields got only 'något hamnade på åkrarna som jordförbättring'; paragraph 1's own list puts murbruk first. C: 'binäring' is glossed in the sheet as 'sysselsättning vid sidan av jordbruket', the burning was scheduled around farming ('bränningen låg om försommaren, när vårbruket var undanstökat') and any one kiln fired 'bara vartannat eller vart tredje år'. The best counsel for C is 'för många hushåll var ugnen den binäring som över huvud taget gav kontanter', but 'the only thing that gave cash' is not 'set farming aside'. D: doubly refuted — 'Berget var däremot sällan något bekymmer, för i de här trakterna gick kalkstenen i dagen', and abandonment in paragraph 6 is caused by the FOREST being cut out. B: carried by paragraph 4 (binäring, kontanter) plus paragraph 7 (kalkverk, cement, 'priset föll under vad ett lag av grannar kunde möta' — outcompeted). Only B survives.
per_question.q4: A (röse positions map old parish boundaries): the lure is the word 'gränsen' in paragraph 6, but the glossary pins the referent — inägor = 'gårdens åkrar och ängar närmast byn', utmark = 'markerna längre bort' — so the boundary is a farm/village-level one INSIDE a parish, and the count itself spans 'Klyvinge med grannsocknar'. Refuted by the unit's own glossary. B: 1924 is given as Klyvinge's last attestable firing and the text makes no comparison of any kind with the neighbouring parishes; the stem's own 'Klyvingetrakten' arguably already includes them, which makes the comparison incoherent as well as unsupported. D: contradicted verbatim — 'Hur gamla de äldsta lämningarna är går inte att avgöra utan utgrävning' — and the negation for the oldest covers the set a fortiori. C: licensed by an explicit succession clause, 'inte sällan flera i rad utmed samma sluttning, äldre ugnar som övergivits när skogen omkring dem huggits ut och ersatts av en yngre ugn längre bort', reinforced by 'Ändå brändes en och samma ugn som regel bara vartannat eller vart tredje år' against the 'sjuttiotal ugnsrester' count. Any degree of succession makes the count overstate simultaneity, so C does not need the strong reading. Only C survives.

findings.disposition: RECORDED, not charged; no key at risk
findings.claim: The wood arithmetic between paragraph 5 and paragraph 8 sits in tension for a domain-informed reader: one firing is said to have consumed more wood than a household used in a whole year, while the reconstruction firing is provisioned with thirteen cubic metres.
findings.evidence: ¶5: 'En enda bränning slukade mer ved än ett hushåll annars gjorde av med på ett år.' ¶8: 'Veden ligger redan travad på platsen: tretton kubikmeter björk, skänkt av markägarna, i väntan på att torka.' A nineteenth-century Swedish farm household's annual firewood ran well above thirteen cubic metres (commonly cited at roughly ten to fifteen famnar, i.e. some 23-35 m3), and a three-to-four-day continuous lime burn of a full charge consumed considerably more than thirteen.
findings.why: This is a friction, not an internal contradiction: the passage never states household consumption in cubic metres, so nothing inside the text is self-refuting, and the museum's kiln may reasonably be smaller than a working one with more wood to follow ('i väntan på att torka'). No option, key or rationale depends on either figure, and no gate tests it. Recorded because an integrated read is exactly where such a seam should surface, and because a reader who knows the domain is the reader this passage is written for. If it is ever touched, raising the coda's figure is cheaper than softening ¶5's comparison, which is doing real rhetorical work.

findings.claim: 'ingen av de ugnar som undersökts visar spår av kol' relies on an anaphora that the archaeological default reading fights: in a kiln context bare 'kol' is charcoal, which every wood-fired kiln must show.
findings.evidence: ¶5: 'förordar för övrigt stenkol som bränsle där sådant fanns att köpa – ett råd som inte tycks ha vunnit gehör, för ingen av de ugnar som undersökts visar spår av kol.' The intended referent is stenkol, supplied fourteen words earlier in the same sentence.
findings.why: The anaphora does license the reading, so this is a precision wobble rather than an error, and it is untested by any question. It is worth recording because the sentence is one of the passage's two law-9 residues (the unheeded coal advice) and residues earn their keep by being crisp. 'visar spår av stenkol' closes it at zero cost.
